name: Aerial-and-earth wireless apparatus
summary: Marconi connected his transmitter and receiver each between a raised wire and the ground, greatly extending the range of wireless telegraph signals.
description: One oscillator terminal connects to earth and the other to an elevated conductor; the receiver similarly connects its coherer between earth and an elevated conductor. Telegraph key, relay and tapping receiver apparatus support signs.
tier_reason: The source verifies the aerial-earth configuration; no0 follows merely because radio otherwise has no0. A broader dependency case is needed for this precise scope. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.
why: Marconi was trying to send telegraph signs without wires over longer distances than laboratory spark apparatus allowed.

places.note: Near Bologna; exact place not given

date.basis: Marconi retrospectively dates the new arrangement to August 1895.

links.statement: Marconi’s 1895 trials progressed through detector and reflector arrangements to the reported August configuration with elevated conductors and earth connections at both ends.
links.alternatives: The preceding Righi-oscillator/reflector arrangement sent directionally but, in Marconi’s account, failed with intervening hills or large obstacles.
links.caveats: This is his retrospective sequence. It does not imply that literal earth connections are required for all wireless systems.
links.timing: Both endpoints anchor to 1895; the source explicitly distinguishes early trials from the August arrangement.
